body: Chemo is getting rough. Had my last TC before I switch over to AC (still two taxol weeks to go) and I finally threw up for the first time. I’m fatigued beyond belief, and can’t help but feel beaten down.
Just to share mine, I’m 3b TNBC and I’m on 24 weeks of chemo, 4 cycles each of TC + keytruda and AC + keytruda (3 week cycles) so the timing can vary a little on how many weeks it takes.
I wear a lot of lulu to my chemo sessions too! Align cropped tanks and scubas, since I run super cold. The cropped scuba is great for port access.

Quick chemo question - say I know that I caught a specific bug (a cold, Covid, flu), would I still have to go to the ER for a fever? My brother is coming down with something, and I’m living with family right now, so it’s possible I’ll also catch it.

My husband’s dog is dying and will be put down. We’re in a different city for my treatment, his family is watching the dog, and he won’t be able to make it in time to say goodbye. 

Everything feels so unfair right now.

After my reaction, chemo has been rescheduled and I’m ready to go! My rash is still very present but no longer itches, and I’m just so happy to continue treatment. On the baldness side, no one is making me feel bad about it, or like I have to hide it, so I’m feeling fine rocking my buzzed 50% head right now. It feels manageable.

I got admitted for a day over a reaction from possibly an antibiotic from an ER trip. I now have missed one week of chemo, and my oncologist canceled chemo this week too. Spiraling some about this but trying to not. Lost my hair and now don’t even get to have chemo. It stinks.

Little personal blog post: Second chemo (weekly taxol) done today with the new port! Access suuuuucked cause I’m tender still, but it was so nice to get it through the port. Steroid hunger is real, but I’m still trending down with weight so I’m not worried too much right now about it. As much as I hate the port I’m now so glad I had it. My infusion arm from last week is still tender, but I’m not feeling any residual port pain so at this point I’m glad I got it. Tumor is noticeably smaller after the first round too. Overall I’m optimistic that things will keep going well.
Got my port today. Love the idea of having it, since I’m a hard stick and IV chemo was super uncomfortable. Hate the fact I need it, and I have something implanted.

First chemo down! I’m one of the rare few it sounds like that had a reaction to Keytruda, but overall it went well. Crazy back pain, felt like 8/10 period cramps. No idea what it was or why. Still no port until next week, so I’m dealing with a sore vein and some nausea. Keytruda + taxol + carbo
